**Published online:**
September 4, 2026

**Geographic focus:**
Japan, USA (G7/G20 context); Asia

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — references July 31 joint intervention and G20 meeting
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BOJ rate hike nearly fully priced in "this month"; yen intervention threat ongoing
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
Japan's top currency diplomat Mimura reaffirmed intervention readiness despite a temporary yen rebound. Markets are nearly fully pricing a BOJ rate hike imminently, supported by hawkish BOJ signals and unusual public pressure from US Treasury Secretary Bessent urging the BOJ to raise rates. Japan's Finance Minister pushed back on the notion of US demands on Japanese monetary policy. The yen remains structurally pressured by wide US-Japan rate differentials, and a prior July 31 joint intervention failed to sustain a yen floor. Bessent notably signaled Washington does not currently view yen moves as disorderly, reducing the likelihood of another joint intervention.
